newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Adelaide Casino sale plan revised.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Adelaide Casino sale plan revised.

text.p: A plan by the South Australia state government to buy Japanese firm Kumagai Gumi Ltd's interest in the Adelaide casino complex for A$6.16 million would not proceed as proposed, it said on Tuesday.

Treasurer Stephen Baker said in a statement that due diligence investigations had revealed a number of legal, financial and planning problems within the complex Adelaide Station and Environs Redevelopment (ASER) complex.
"As a result ... the government has resolved not to proceed with the purchase of Kumagai's interest as proposed," he said.
Instead, he said the government was working with Kumagai and the Superannuation Funds Management Corporation (SFMC) to address the problems and restructure the ASER complex.

Baker said the corporate structure problems, the impact of gaming machines in hotels and clubs, and the opening of casinos in other states had resulted in the SFMC taking a further provision of A$31.2 million on its exposure to ASER.

"While the key components of the ASER group - the Adelaide Casino, the Hyatt hotel, and the Riverside (office) building - continue to operate profitably before interest and tax, the revenue flows are proving insufficient to service the interest
payments on the heavily debt burdened structure," he said.
Baker said the government still intended eventually to put the ASER complex up for sale.
